## [§5.3.b] Trial with penalty — definition and logic

I call it a trial. with penalty. That sounds ugly. That's how I' call it internally. You wouldn't say that to somebody. But it's a trial with penalty. So basically, a customer can try out your product or service for free so long as they meet your terms. For comparison, the win-your-money-back offer, the attraction offer, gives customers the chance to get their money back if they meet the terms. In a trial with penalty offer, customers only pay if they don't meet the terms. So the win-your-money-back and the free trial with penalty are virtually the same offer; we're just changing when they pay and how they pay. So they'll mirror the actions and results that you used in win-your-money-back, but this time, we use avoiding fees rather than winning your money back as the incentive for adherence. So they avoid penalties rather than get or losing their money that they paid originally. All right, so with a trial with penalty, this isn't, "Here's my thing, see if you like it." It's, "Here's my thing. You get it for free so long as you do this stuff, which makes you a perfect fit for my next offer. And if you don't, then you have to pay for it." So it's kind of like a win-win for you, because if they don't do it, then they pay. And if they do do it, then they're gonna be really likely to buy the next thing. Now, I'm gonna give you something like, "Wait, so if they don't do it, then they pay, and they didn't wanna pay originally?" I'll cover how to get around that weirdness. Let's say you normally close three out of 10 people on your attraction offer, and now you downsell another four on a trial with penalty. Then, after the trial finishes, you upsell three of them. So you go from three sales to six sales, which doubles your customers. I use this as a downsell, but it could also be used as a front end. So I don't prefer to advertise this; I prefer to present this after someone already said no to giving me money. Some people advertise this as how they get customers. It's up to you. Obviously, that HR company advertised it as how they get customers. So if you really wanna help people, convincing them to put some skin in the game is a great way to do it. And so one of my sales rules is that everyone buys something who's qualified. And so I love that as a concept. It's like everyone should buy. Like, if they're qualified and we have the thing, every person should buy. The terms may change, but everyone should buy. So, here's the difference between trials and penalties and rebates. A trial is they j- you just get a card and then bill them later. A penalty/incentive is you get a card and bill later and also if they don't complete their activation activities. So the fees are associated with non-consumption and not showing up to other sales consultations. Remember the four things we had in the win-your-money-back is you wanna have them advertise your business, you wanna have them show up for sales consults, you wanna do things that, um, that get them results, and... There's another one. I can't remember what it was, but there's four, and those are the main ones. All right? So you want to associate them doing the things that gets them results, because if they get results, then they'll probably wanna buy. All right? So they're not here' for a trial; they're here to solve a problem, so solve it, because trials don't do anything. Them taking action is just what's going to solve their problem. And if someone has a problem with that, it's an easy thing to get around. Think about the logic. If someone says, "I'm not willing to commit to that," you're like, "Well, do you want the outcome?" They're gonna say yes. It's like, "Well, you have to do this stuff to get the outcome." So if you don't, if you don't plan on doing this stuff, then you're never going to get the outcome. This is just the easiest way that I can give you all this service for free. If you really do wanna do this, "I do wanna do this," great, then you're not gonna pay anything, 'cause you're gonna follow through, and this just gives you added incentive to do it. And if this doesn't work for you, then certainly nothing else will.
